claim.pdf_says: BLOCK CONTAINS [integer-1 TO] integer-2 {RECORDS / CHARACTERS} -- RECORDS is underlined, CHARACTERS is NOT underlined
claim.why_it_matters: Format 3 FD BLOCK CONTAINS clause: underlining added to CHARACTERS, the same defect as p531-1.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of page 533 (X-17, Inter-Program Communication FD Format 3) shows the BLOCK CONTAINS choice braces stacking RECORDS, which is underlined, above CHARACTERS, which is not. Lines 14-16 of page-533.md show both <u>RECORDS</u> and <u>CHARACTERS</u>. Underlining marks a required key word. Under §1985:IV.2.1.4, braces without choice indicators allow the selected option to be implicitly selected, so a non-underlined CHARACTERS can be omitted (BLOCK CONTAINS n with CHARACTERS implied). The markdown underlines it and so turns an optional word into a required one. That is a normative notation discrepancy, and the claim quotes both sources correctly.
